stages.title: What the Chat Is Doing
stages.description: A chat tool is a large language model: a network trained on text, usually to predict the next word, then tuned to follow instructions.
learningObjectives: Define a large language model
Separate pretraining from instruction tuning
Say what a generative model produces
Name a few jobs the model is built for, and the limit of a plausible sentence

explainBack.question: Someone treats the chat box like a database that looks up the right fact. Explain what the model was trained to do, and what kind of thing it is generating.
rubric: A large language model is a neural network trained on a vast amount of text, especially for generating language
Modern chatbots such as ChatGPT, Claude, and Gemini are built on these models
A generative pre-trained transformer is pretrained to predict the next word, then often fine-tuned to follow instructions
Before that fine-tuning, most of these models are next-token predictors; biased or inaccurate training data makes the output less reliable
Generative AI produces new text, images, or other data from patterns in its training data, in response to a prompt

resources.title: Large language model
resources.description: What an LLM is, how GPT-style models are trained, and what inference means.
keyPoints: A large language model is typically a neural network trained on a vast amount of text for language tasks, especially generation
These models are the basis of chatbots such as ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini, Grok, and DeepSeek
They are typically transformers; a generative pre-trained transformer is pretrained to predict the next word, then often fine-tuned to follow instructions
Before fine-tuning, most LLMs are next-token predictors; fine-tuning can use instruction tuning or reinforcement learning from human feedback
Biased or inaccurate training data can make the output less reliable; inference is sending an input and receiving generated text or other files

resources.title: Introduction to Generative AI
resources.description: Google Cloud's short course on what generative AI produces and what a prompt is.
keyPoints: Generative AI creates new content from patterns it learned in existing content
A generative language model predicts what comes next and can produce new combinations of text
Large language models are one type of generative AI
A prompt is a short piece of text given to the model as input, and it is how you steer the output

resources.title: Introduction to Large Language Models
resources.description: Google Cloud's introduction to what an LLM is trained to do and how the kinds of models differ.
keyPoints: Large language models are large, general-purpose language models that are pretrained and then fine-tuned
They are a subset of deep learning and are used for classification, question answering, summarization, and text generation
They are almost exclusively based on transformer models
The course separates generic language models, instruction-tuned models, and dialog-tuned models, and each kind is prompted differently

stages.title: A Prompt That Names the Job
stages.description: Say what you want, who it is for, and what the answer should look like. An example beats a vague request.
learningObjectives: State the task, the constraints, and the output format
Add the reason for a rule when the rule would otherwise look arbitrary
Use an example when the shape of the answer matters
Tell a zero-shot prompt from a prompt that includes examples

explainBack.question: Your prompt is 'write something about our product.' Rewrite the idea of that prompt, and explain why the vague version fails.
rubric: A prompt is the input that asks the model for a response; its quality changes the output
Be specific about the output format and the constraints; show the prompt to a colleague, and if they would be confused, the model will be too
Explaining why a rule matters helps the model more than a bare 'never'
A few relevant, diverse examples are one of the most reliable ways to steer format and tone
Zero-shot is an instruction with no example; few-shot gives one or more input-output examples first

resources.title: Prompting best practices
resources.description: Anthropic's current guide: clear instructions, context, examples, and a role.
keyPoints: Be clear and direct; specify the output format and the constraints instead of hoping the model infers them
The golden rule is to show the prompt to a colleague with little context; if they would be confused, the model will be too
Explain why a behavior matters; the model can generalize from the reason
Examples are one of the most reliable ways to steer format, tone, and structure; make them relevant, diverse, and easy to tell apart from the instructions
A role, even one sentence in the system prompt, focuses behavior and tone

resources.title: Prompt engineering: overview and guide
resources.description: What a prompt is, and the difference between asking with no example and asking with several.
keyPoints: Prompt engineering is designing prompts so a model understands the intent and produces the response you want
A prompt is the input, from a short question to instructions, code, or a writing sample
Context and examples in the prompt help the model match the task
Zero-shot prompting is a direct instruction with no example, such as 'summarize this'
Few-shot prompting gives one or more examples of the desired input and output before the real request; chain-of-thought asks the model to show intermediate steps

resources.title: Tips to becoming a world-class Prompt Engineer
resources.description: A short Google Cloud video: specific instructions, context, examples, and a persona.
keyPoints: Prompt engineering here means using natural language to ask a large language model to summarize, generate, or review
Be specific: 'blueberry muffins' does not say that you need fifty and that they must be vegan
Add context so the model can interpret the request
Examples give the model a frame, and trying a persona is one way to retune the prompt

stages.title: Check the Answer Before You Use It
stages.description: A fluent answer can still be false. The model can invent a citation and present it as a fact.
learningObjectives: Define an AI hallucination
Expect fabricated citations
Treat a confident tone as unrelated to truth
Check claims that matter against a source you trust

explainBack.question: The model gives you a quotation, a paper title, and a confident explanation. Explain what can be wrong with that answer, and what you would do before you repeat it.
rubric: A hallucination is a response that contains false or misleading information presented as fact
Chatbots can embed plausible falsehoods, including fabricated citations
OpenAI has described the tendency as inventing facts in moments of uncertainty, and as fabricating information while behaving as if stating facts
The term is disputed because it compares the model to a person; the failure is still a false or misleading output
High-stakes uses, including medical diagnostics, are where an unchecked error does the most harm, so a claim you will rely on has to be checked against a source

resources.title: Hallucination (artificial intelligence)
resources.description: What researchers and labs mean when a model states something that is not true.
keyPoints: In AI, a hallucination is a response that contains false or misleading information presented as fact
Large-language-model chatbots may embed plausible-sounding falsehoods, such as fabricated citations
Definitions in use include inventing facts in moments of uncertainty and fabricating information while behaving as if stating facts
Some engineers object to the word because it treats the computer like a person; symbolic systems generally do not fail this way
The practical problem is reliability in high-stakes work, including medical diagnostics, where a confident error is costly

stages.title: Writing With a Model
stages.description: Using a model to help write is allowed. Publishing a pile of pages mainly to rank is not. Say how the page was made when a reader would ask.
learningObjectives: Separate assistive use from spam
Keep a person responsible for the original value
Add a byline when readers would ask who wrote it
Disclose automation when readers would ask how it was made

explainBack.question: You used a chat model to draft a post, then rewrote it from your own notes. Explain how that differs from generating dozens of pages to chase search traffic, and when you would tell the reader a model was involved.
rubric: Google ranks by the quality of the content, not by whether a person or a tool produced it
Automation, including AI, used mainly to manipulate search rankings violates the spam policies
Automation has long produced useful pages such as scores, forecasts, and transcripts; AI can also help a person make original work
Using AI does not give a page a special ranking boost; if it is not useful, original, and trustworthy, it may not do well
Use an accurate human byline where readers would ask who wrote it, and disclose AI where they would ask how it was created; do not list the model as the author

resources.title: Google Search's guidance about AI-generated content
resources.description: Google's 2023 note: quality matters more than whether a tool helped write the page.
keyPoints: Ranking systems aim to reward original, high-quality content; the focus is the quality, not how the content was produced
Using automation, including AI, primarily to manipulate rankings violates the spam policies
Not all automation is spam; scores, weather, and transcripts have long been generated, and AI can help people make useful pages
Using AI does not give content any special gain in Search
Consider a byline where a reader would ask who wrote it, disclose automation where they would ask how it was made, and do not list the AI as the author

stages.title: What You Paste Into the Box
stages.description: Text you paste is part of the prompt. Hidden instructions in a page or a file can change what the model does, including what it repeats.
learningObjectives: Separate a direct prompt injection from an indirect one
Treat a webpage or file you ask the model to read as untrusted input
Name disclosure of sensitive information as one possible result
Keep a person in the loop before a high-risk action

explainBack.question: You paste a long webpage into the chat and ask for a summary. Explain how that page can change the model's behavior, and what you should not have put in the same conversation.
rubric: Prompt injection is input that alters the model's behavior or output in a way you did not intend
A direct injection is in the prompt you type; an indirect injection is hidden in outside content such as a website or a file the model reads
The instructions do not have to be visible to a person, as long as the model parses them
One listed outcome is disclosure of sensitive information, including material from the conversation
A practical mitigation is to mark untrusted content as separate from your instructions, and to require a person to approve high-risk actions

resources.title: LLM01:2025 Prompt Injection
resources.description: How a prompt, or a page you asked the model to read, can redirect the model.
keyPoints: Prompt injection is user input that alters the model's behavior or output in unintended ways
The input does not have to be readable by a person; it only has to be parsed by the model
Direct injection is in the prompt itself; indirect injection arrives in external content such as a website or a file
Effects include disclosing sensitive information, manipulating the content, and triggering actions the model is connected to
Mitigations include separating untrusted content from the instructions and requiring human approval for high-risk actions; a complete prevention is not claimed

stages.title: Pictures the Model Draws
stages.description: An image model makes a new picture from patterns in its training data. The picture can look like a photograph of something that never happened.
learningObjectives: Define generative AI beyond chat text
Name image and video tools as the same family of model
Treat a generated scene as invented unless you have another source
Remember that training data has included copyrighted works

explainBack.question: A generated picture shows a famous bridge with a second track and a train on the wrong side. Explain what the model was doing, and why you would not publish that frame as a photo of the place.
rubric: Generative AI uses models to produce text, images, video, audio, code, or other data from patterns in training data, usually from a prompt
Text-to-image tools such as DALL-E, Firefly, Stable Diffusion, and Midjourney, and text-to-video tools such as Sora, are in this family
A generated picture can add details that are not in the real scene; the Glenfinnan example shows a second track and trains running on the wrong side
The same systems are used for deepfakes and fake news, so a realistic frame is not evidence
Generative models have been trained on copyrighted works without the rightholders' permission

resources.title: Generative artificial intelligence
resources.description: The wider field: text, images, video, and the harms that come with realistic output.
keyPoints: Generative AI produces text, images, video, audio, code, or other data by learning patterns in training data and responding to a prompt
Chatbots are one application; text-to-image models include DALL-E, Firefly, Stable Diffusion, and Midjourney, and text-to-video models include Sora
The same tools have been used for fake news and deepfakes
Models have been trained on copyrighted works without the rightholders' permission

resources.title: Hallucination (artificial intelligence)
resources.description: A generated video of a real viaduct that invents tracks, direction, and the shape of the train.
keyPoints: A generated video of the Glenfinnan Viaduct shows a second track, trains running on the right instead of the left, and a carriage bending as it turns
The real viaduct and the real train do not match that generated frame
The word hallucination covers false or misleading output presented as if it were real, including in images and video
A realistic generated scene is not a record of the place

stages.title: When the Tool Is the Wrong Tool
stages.description: The model continues a likely sentence. That is a bad instrument for a dose, a statute, a price, or any fact you cannot afford to invent.
learningObjectives: Connect a wrong answer to next-token prediction
Refuse to treat the chat as a source for medicine or other high-stakes facts
Ask for the source and then open that source
Prefer a calculator, a current official page, or a person when the cost of being wrong is high

explainBack.question: A classmate wants the model to decide a medicine dose and to quote the law that allows it. Explain why this is the wrong tool, using how the model produces text.
rubric: Before instruction tuning, most large language models are trained to predict the next token, not to look a fact up in a database
A fluent answer can still be a falsehood presented as fact, including a fabricated citation
Medical diagnostics is one of the high-stakes settings where that failure is dangerous
Biased or inaccurate training data makes the output less reliable, and a tool such as web search is an add-on, not a guarantee
The check is to leave the chat and confirm the claim in a source that is actually responsible for it

resources.title: Large language model
resources.description: The training objective: predict the next word, then shape the behavior with fine-tuning.
keyPoints: GPT-style models are pretrained to predict the next word
Before fine-tuning, most LLMs are next-token predictors
Instruction tuning and reinforcement learning from human feedback change how the model behaves; they do not turn it into a database
Biased or inaccurate training data can make the output less reliable
A software harness can add tools such as web search; that is separate from the model's own generation

resources.title: Hallucination (artificial intelligence)
resources.description: Why a made-up citation or a made-up medical claim is a known failure, not a rare glitch.
keyPoints: Hallucinated output includes fabricated citations presented as real
Detecting those errors is hard enough that high-stakes deployment is a known problem
Medical diagnostics is named among the settings where a false answer does serious harm
A confident tone is part of the failure: the model behaves as if it is stating facts

stages.title: Who Owns What Comes Back
stages.description: In the United States, copyright needs a human author. Typing a prompt is not enough. A human's own writing and a human's creative edit can still be protected.
learningObjectives: State the human-authorship requirement
Explain why a prompt alone does not make you the author of the output
Name the human contributions the Copyright Office says can still count
Keep the model off the author line

explainBack.question: You typed a detailed prompt and want to register the picture the model returned, with the model listed as co-author. Explain what the U.S. Copyright Office says can be protected, and what cannot.
rubric: U.S. copyright protects original expression created by a human author
Generative output is protected only where a human has determined sufficient expressive elements
A human-authored work that remains perceptible in the output, or a human's creative arrangement or modification of the output, can qualify; the mere provision of prompts does not
Using AI to assist, or including AI material inside a larger human-authored work, does not by itself bar copyright in the human part
Do not list the AI tool or the company that provides it as an author

resources.title: Copyright and Artificial Intelligence
resources.description: The Office's hub for its report on AI outputs, training, and digital replicas.
keyPoints: The Copyright Office has been examining copyright in AI-generated works and the use of copyrighted material in training
Part 2 of the report, published on 29 January 2025, addresses whether outputs created with generative AI can be copyrighted
Part 1 addresses digital replicas; a pre-publication Part 3 addresses training on copyrighted works
The human-authorship question is the Office's, not a setting inside the chat tool

resources.title: Copyright and Artificial Intelligence, Part 2: Copyrightability
resources.description: The Office's January 2025 conclusion: prompts alone do not make the output yours.
keyPoints: Outputs of generative AI can be protected only where a human author has determined sufficient expressive elements
That can include a human-authored work perceptible in the output, or a human's creative arrangement or modification of the output
The mere provision of prompts is not enough
Using AI as an aid, or placing AI-generated material inside a larger human-authored work, does not bar copyright in the human contribution
The Office did not recommend a new law to give extra protection to AI-generated outputs

name: AI Tools
description: Learn to put a chat model on a real task: what it is predicting, how to write the prompt, how to check the answer, what you paste in, and what copyright does not give you.
